acceptance: Find an approach whose job time is measured lower on CI over several runs, not only locally
Collection evidence and the shard coverage check are unchanged
context: Merged PR #3443: medium-collect restores tests/**/__pycache__ and benchbox/**/__pycache__ via actions/cache (keyed on uv.lock plus source hashes, prefix restore keys) and runs compileall --invalidation-mode checked-hash before collection; collection command, marker expression, shard-count check and evidence upload unchanged; documented exemption added in the CI lint-parity test. Local macOS measurement only: cold 24.1s vs 13.9s warm for the same collect command. NOT verified: any CI timing, cache hit rate or cache size on hosted runners. Acceptance (lower job time across several CI runs, identical collection evidence) needs observation of runs after merge; item stays open for that.
description: medium-collect (ci.yml) is on the critical path: every medium shard needs it. Over the 18 most recent completed PR runs its job time was 119-183 s (median 154 s), of which the 'Collect the complete medium tier' step was a median 108 s (max 131 s), checkout 15 s (fetch-depth 0), dependency install 21 s. Locally the same command (pytest --collect-only -q -n 0 -m <medium expression>, 46,519 tests collected, 31,752 deselected, 14,767 kept) took 13.4 s with a warm __pycache__ and 49.9 s after deleting tests/**/__pycache__, so the cost is mostly compiling and assertion-rewriting the test modules on a fresh checkout, not the marker selection. The unit job already avoids this with a 'Pre-build the assertion-rewrite cache' step that collects the test files in nproc parallel chunks (ci.yml around line 817); medium-collect has no such step and collects single-process (-n 0). Directory-level timings with a warm cache: tests/unit 13 s (12,192 medium), tests/integration 4 s (1,181), everything else under 3 s combined.
